task.title: Behaviour-preserving refactor of kvparse.parser
task.statement: Refactor kvparse/parser.py without changing any behaviour. Two changes are requested. (1) parse_line(line) must be rewritten without the hand-rolled index loops: split the line at the first '=' with str.partition, strip the key and the value, raise ValueError when there is no '=' or the stripped key is empty, and remove one pair of matching surrounding quotes (both ends '"' or both ends "'") from a stripped value of length two or more; the function must not contain a 'while' loop. (2) Extract the detection of ignorable lines into a module-level function _is_ignorable(line) -> bool in kvparse/parser.py that returns True exactly when the stripped line is empty or starts with '#' or ';', and make parse use it. The observable behaviour of parse and parse_line must stay byte-for-byte identical for every str input: the same return values, the same exception types in the same situations (TypeError for non-string input to parse, ValueError for a malformed line), later duplicate keys still win, and quotes are removed only when the stripped value starts and ends with the same quote character (a value like '"x\'' keeps both characters; a lone '"' is kept). Exception messages are not prescribed. parse keeps raising TypeError for non-string input; what parse_line does with a non-string argument (for example a list or a mapping) is unspecified and must not be tested, because the required use of str.partition changes it. Keep the public names parse and parse_line exported from kvparse, do not modify the tests, and keep the existing suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: parse_line raises ValueError for '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=' and '\t= 1'.

parse behaviour unchanged: comments ('#' or ';' as the first non-blank character), blank lines and Windows line endings are handled as before; later duplicate keys win; parse('') == {}; parse('k = v') == {'k': 'v'}.
parse raises ValueError for a malformed line anywhere in the text and TypeError for non-string input (None, 3, a list, bytes).
kvparse.parser._is_ignorable exists, returns True for '   # c', '' and '\t; c', and False for 'a = 1' and 'a = # not a comment'.
The source of parse_line contains no 'while' loop and uses str.partition.
The existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged.
Unspecified, not to be tested: parse_line with a non-string argument.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse_line
interface_contract.behavior: For a str input, return a two-element tuple of strings. Split at the first '=' using str.partition (line.partition('=') is acceptable). Strip both resulting key and value using Python's default str.strip semantics. After stripping, remove exactly one outer character from each end of the value only if its length is at least two and both characters are matching single quotes or matching double quotes. Preserve everything inside that pair without further stripping or unescaping. Remain importable as kvparse.parse_line.
error_cases: ValueError: the key before the first '=' is empty after stripping.
Behavior for non-string arguments is unspecified and must not be tested.
Exception message text is not prescribed.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse
interface_contract.behavior: Accept input satisfying isinstance(text, str) and return a dict mapping parsed string keys to string values. Iterate over text.splitlines() using its existing default semantics. Use _is_ignorable to skip blank lines and lines whose first non-whitespace character is '#' or ';'. Pass each remaining raw line to parse_line and assign its result into the dictionary in input order, so later duplicate keys replace earlier values without moving the key's dictionary position. Remain importable as kvparse.parse.
error_cases: TypeError: text is not an instance of str, including None, integers, lists, and bytes.
ValueError: any non-ignored line is malformed according to parse_line; no partial dictionary is returned.
Exception message text is not prescribed.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser._is_ignorable
interface_contract.behavior: Module-level helper for string lines. Return True exactly when line.strip() is empty or begins with '#' or ';'; otherwise return False. Return a bool. The helper is internal and need not be exported from kvparse.
error_cases: Behavior for non-string arguments is unspecified and must not be tested.

acceptance_criteria: 1. parse_line('a=b') == ('a', 'b'); parse_line(' a = b ') == ('a', 'b'); parse_line('a==b') == ('a', '=b'); parse_line('a = b = c') == ('a', 'b = c'); parse_line('a=') == ('a', '').
3. parse_line('q = "x\'') == ('q', '"x\''); parse_line('q = "') == ('q', '"'); a lone single quote is likewise preserved. Mismatched outer quotes are never removed.

4. parse_line('q = " spaced "') == ('q', ' spaced '); parse_line('k e y = v') == ('k e y', 'v'); parse_line('u = "a" "b"') == ('u', 'a" "b'). Quote removal occurs once, with no recursive removal, unescaping, or subsequent stripping.
5. parse_line raises ValueError for each of '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=', and '\t= 1'. More generally, every string lacking '=' or having an empty stripped key raises ValueError.

6. Default str.strip semantics are preserved, including Unicode whitespace. Keys retain internal whitespace and quotes. Values retain internal whitespace, additional equals signs, backslashes, and comment markers.

7. parse_line treats its argument as one string, without splitting lines or skipping comments: parse_line('#k=v') == ('#k', 'v'), and embedded line separators are retained unless removed as surrounding whitespace by strip.

8. _is_ignorable returns True for '', '   ', '   # c', and '\t; c'; it returns False for 'a = 1', 'a = # not a comment', and 'a = ; not a comment'. For all string inputs its result matches the specified stripped-empty-or-comment-prefix rule.

9. parse('') == {}; parse('k = v') == {'k': 'v'}; parse('# comment

') == {'name': 'x'}. Whitespace-prefixed comments and whitespace-only lines are ignored, including comment lines containing '='.
10. parse preserves text.splitlines() semantics, including CRLF, lone CR, LF, and other Python-recognized line separators. For example, parse('a=1\r\nb=2\r\n') == {'a': '1', 'b': '2'}.
11. Later duplicate stripped keys win: parse(' a = 1\nb=2\na=3') == {'a': '3', 'b': '2'}, with dictionary iteration order ['a', 'b']. Keys remain case-sensitive.
12. Inline comment markers are ordinary value content: parse('a = # not a comment\nb = ; also a value') == {'a': '# not a comment', 'b': '; also a value'}.
13. parse raises ValueError when a malformed non-ignored line occurs at the beginning, middle, or end of otherwise valid text. Ignored comment lines need not contain '='.
14. parse raises TypeError for None, 3, [], and b'a=b', and retains its isinstance(text, str) input guard. No assertions constrain exception messages.
15. Source inspection confirms that parse_line uses str.partition to split at the first '=' and contains no while loop or replacement hand-written index-scanning loops.
16. Source inspection confirms that _is_ignorable is defined at module level with return annotation bool and that parse calls it to determine which lines to skip.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion is never overridden. The classification itself remains a model judgement.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.
